newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton cleared by one grand jury - report.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton cleared by one grand jury - report.

text.p: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton has been cleared by the grand jury that questioned her for more than four hours last year on Whitewater-related matters, CBS News reported on Wednesday.
The network quoted an unidentified source close to the grand jury as saying, "I'm not sure what's going on in Arkansas, but I give you my word, there is no indictment of her here in Washington."

Independent counsel Kenneth Starr convened two grand juries to investigate the Whitewater affair, a complex web of Arkansas business deals involving the Clintons and allegations of cover-up at the White House.

The Washington grand jury met for 18 months and dealt with questions of possible Whitewater-related wrongdoing, along with other issues, by the Clintons after they moved into the White House in January, 1993.
The Little Rock grand jury is examining the original 1978 Whitewater land deal -- and subsequent events in Arkansas -- in which the Clintons were partners with James and Susan McDougal.

Although their investment lost money, questions have arisen about whether funds for the project and for Clinton's gubernatorial campaign were siphoned from the failed Madison Savings and Loan Association, which McDougal also ran.
Neither President nor Mrs Clinton has been accused of any wrongdoing in Starr's long-running investigation.

Hillary Clinton was summoned before the Washington grand jury in January last year to answer questions about the mysterious appearance in the private White House family quarters of legal billing records sought for two years by Whitewater investigators. It was the first time that a U.S. first lady had appeared before such a tribunal.
The source quoted by CBS declined to say if the grand jury had voted to indict Webster Hubbell, former associate attorney general and a close friend of the Clintons.

Hubbell resigned from the Justice Department in 1994 and was jailed in 1995 after pleading guilty to fraudulent billing of clients at the Rose law firm in Little Rock before he joined the Clinton administration. He and Hillary Clinton were partners at the firm.

Questions have arisen about payments Hubbell received after he resigned from people with close ties to Clinton, leading critics to ask if they were intended as "hush money" to keep him from saying what he knew about the Whitewater case.
